hook: MS brain shrinkage tracks the wiring: hub regions and their linked neighbors lose the most tissue
hook_turn: hub regions and their linked neighbors lose the most tissue
summary: In 2187 MRI scans, gray matter loss in multiple sclerosis followed brain connectivity. Regions that act as network hubs, and regions wired to already damaged areas, shrank most, which fits the idea that damage spreads along connections. Network measures also improved prediction of later shrinkage. The data are associations from imaging, so they cannot prove the spread mechanism.
title: The role of network connectivity and transcriptomic vulnerability in shaping gray matter atrophy in multiple sclerosis.
